claims.statement: On September 8, 2026, Kodiak reported its long-haul driverless Autonomy Readiness Measure at 93% through August 2026, up from 91% through July. It still targeted launch by the end of 2026.
claims.text: On September 8, 2026, Kodiak reported its long-haul driverless Autonomy Readiness Measure at 93% through August 2026, up from 91% through July. It still targeted launch by the end of 2026.
claims.quote:
September 8, 2026
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., -- Kodiak AI, Inc. (“Kodiak”) (Nasdaq: KDK), a leading provider of Physical AI-powered autonomous driving technology, today reaffirmed that it remains on track to launch driverless long-haul commercial service by the end of 2026. The company's Autonomy Readiness Measure ("ARM") for long-haul driverless operations reached 93% at the end of August 2026, up from 91% at the end of July.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI On Track For Year-End Driverless Long-Haul Launch as Safety Case Readiness Reaches 93%
claims.quote_note: Publication dateline followed by first body paragraph; newline separates the source blocks.

claims.statement: Kodiak defines ARM as the percentage of safety-case claims and evidence materially complete. This measures safety-case completion, not a probability of a safe trip.
claims.text: Kodiak defines ARM as the percentage of safety-case claims and evidence materially complete. This measures safety-case completion, not a probability of a safe trip.
claims.quote: Kodiak’s ARM measures the percentage of claims and evidence in Kodiak’s safety case for driverless operations that are materially complete. The increase to 93% reflects consistent progress in the remaining development, testing and validation activities required to safely launch the Kodiak Driver into long-haul driverless service.
claims.interpretation_note: The probability distinction follows from the company’s explicit metric definition; it is explanatory analysis, not a direct company quote.

claims.statement: Kodiak says remaining work is concentrated on final engineering verification and validation; completion of the safety case and driverless long-haul launch before year end remain expectations.
claims.text: Kodiak says remaining work is concentrated on final engineering verification and validation; completion of the safety case and driverless long-haul launch before year end remain expectations.
claims.quote: We have identified and scheduled the remaining work, which is concentrated on final engineering verification and validation activities. We expect to complete the safety case before year’s end and launch driverless long-haul service.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI safety-case progress release, CEO Don Burnette quotation

claims.statement: Kodiak’s June 9, 2026 prospectus names Texas as the initial planned long-haul driverless deployment market, after extending the safety case to that domain.
claims.text: Kodiak’s June 9, 2026 prospectus names Texas as the initial planned long-haul driverless deployment market, after extending the safety case to that domain.
claims.quote:
The date of this prospectus is June 9, 2026.
Following the expansion of our safety case to cover the long-haul operating domain, we plan to launch our long-haul driverless deployment initially in Texas.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI, Inc., June 9, 2026 Form 424B3 prospectus, Business commercialization section
claims.quote_note: First sentence is the cover-page date; second is the Business section. Separate excerpts are separated by a newline. Geography is the June plan, not newly specified September 8.

claims.statement: Kodiak reported in May that trucks using its autonomous technology began hauling Roehl freight between Dallas and Houston in April 2026. This is existing freight-service context; the same May release still described driverless long-haul operations as a future goal.
claims.text: Kodiak reported in May that trucks using its autonomous technology began hauling Roehl freight between Dallas and Houston in April 2026. This is existing freight-service context; the same May release still described driverless long-haul operations as a future goal.
claims.quote:
May 7, 2026
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., May 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kodiak AI, Inc. ("Kodiak”) (Nasdaq: KDK), a leading provider of Physical AI-powered autonomous vehicle technology, today announced it is autonomously hauling freight with Roehl Transport, one of America’s leading truckload carriers. Starting in April 2026, trucks equipped with the Kodiak Driver, Kodiak’s autonomous system, began hauling freight between Dallas and Houston four times roundtrip per week for Roehl Transport.
Kodiak continues to make progress toward closing its long-haul safety case and launching driverless operations by the end of 2026.
claims.source_title: Kodiak Begins Hauling Freight Autonomously With Roehl Transport
claims.quote_note: Dateline, first body paragraph, and final body paragraph opening sentence are separated by newlines.

claims.statement: Kodiak uses distinct safety cases for each operating environment; the highway launch safety case remains under completion. A safety case is a structured argument supported by evidence about safe operation in a defined operating environment.
claims.text: Kodiak uses distinct safety cases for each operating environment; the highway launch safety case remains under completion. A safety case is a structured argument supported by evidence about safe operation in a defined operating environment.
claims.quote:
In preparation for driverless long-haul operations, Kodiak is completing work on its highway launch safety case. Kodiak’s safety case is a structured argument, supported by evidence, that the Kodiak Driver, the company's autonomous driving system, can operate safely in a defined operating environment.
The Kodiak Driver uses a single AI architecture across use cases, with a distinct safety case for each operating environment.
claims.quote_note: Two separate source paragraphs, separated by newline.

rejected.claim: The truck is ready for a road its safety case has not cleared.
rejected.reason: Source does not establish readiness of a particular truck or clearance of a particular road; engineering verification remains. Replaced with incomplete highway-launch safety case.

rejected.claim: The reported 93% is a 93% chance of a safe trip, independent safety certification, or regulatory launch approval.
rejected.reason: Company explicitly defines the metric as safety-case claims and evidence materially complete; no independent verification or regulatory approval is supplied.

rejected.claim: Driverless long-haul service already launched on Dallas–Houston, or Dallas County is the announced initial driverless launch location.
rejected.reason: Dallas–Houston is historical freight context; Texas-wide initial driverless geography comes from the June prospectus, with no initial route or county specified.

rejected.claim: Final verification and validation still come next.
rejected.reason: Implies those activities have not begun. Source says remaining work is concentrated there. Repaired to still remain.
September 8 is announcement date; metric is measured at August end.

rejected.claim: Atlas early-2027 public-road expansion is Kodiak’s year-end highway launch.
rejected.reason: Different programs and timelines. Atlas page was refetched but these figures are excluded.
